descriptionChirho: To show, demonstrate, or point out something to someone, making visible or evident what was previously unknown. Covers both future ('I will show') and aorist ('I showed') tense forms of the same demonstrative meaning. Multilingual translations confirm consistent 'show' semantics: Spanish 'mostraré/os mostré,' Arabic 'سَأُرِيكُمْ/أَرَيْتُكُمْ' (I will show you / I showed you), Hindi 'दिखाऊँगा/दिखाया' (will show / showed), Korean '보여주겠다/보여주었다' (will show / showed), Swahili 'nitawaonyesha/niliwaonyesha' (I will show them / I showed them).

To warn or forewarn someone, pointing out danger or consequence as a cautionary admonition rather than a neutral demonstration. Distinguished from the 'show' sense by Swahili 'aliwaonya' (he warned them, using the warning-specific verb '-onya'), and Arabic 'أَنْذَرَكُمْ' (he warned you, from the root ن-ذ-ر for warning). Spanish 'os mostró' and Korean '보여줬나' retain the 'show' gloss, but the Swahili and Arabic evidence reveals the warning/admonitory force present in certain Lukan contexts (Luke 3:7, Matt 3:7).
